defects.description: Capacity enforcement evicts while the size is `>=` capacity instead of strictly greater, so the cache tops out at capacity-1 live entries and discards a valid entry one insertion too early.
paraphrases: The eviction loop fires the moment the store reaches its limit rather than after surpassing it, permanently costing the cache one slot of its advertised size.
Filling the cache to exactly N entries immediately triggers a removal, so a cache configured for N never actually retains N items.
Because the condition includes equality, the least-recently-used entry is thrown out prematurely whenever the count merely equals the bound.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        while len(self._store) > self._capacity:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: Expiry uses strict `>` against the deadline instead of `>=`, so an entry read at exactly its expiration instant is still reported as live rather than expired.
paraphrases: At the precise clock value where an entry's deadline lands it should count as stale, but the strict comparison keeps it valid for that tick.
A lookup arriving exactly on `expires_at` returns the cached value instead of a miss, so entries survive one instant past their intended lifetime.
The deadline is treated as still-fresh because expiry requires the clock to advance strictly beyond it rather than reach it.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        return self.expires_at is not None and now >= self.expires_at'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The hit_rate property divides misses by total lookups instead of hits, so it reports the miss fraction under the name hit_rate and propagates the wrong value into as_dict() and __repr__.
paraphrases: The success ratio is derived from the miss counter, so a cache serving mostly hits advertises a deceptively low figure.
What the property returns is really the fraction of lookups that failed, making every stats snapshot show the complement of the true value.
The numerator names the wrong tally — misses where hits belong — inverting the meaning of the reported effectiveness metric.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        return (self.hits / total) if total else 0.0'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: delete() returns the negation of what it should: checking `is None` makes it report True when the key was absent (nothing removed) and False when an entry was actually deleted.
paraphrases: The boolean result of the removal is flipped, so callers are told a deletion succeeded exactly when nothing was there to delete.
Deleting a present key yields False while deleting a missing key yields True, because the presence test is written against None instead of not-None.
The return value contradicts the documented 'whether anything was deleted' — a real removal signals false and a no-op signals true.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '            return self._store.pop(key, None) is not None'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: `__contains__` delegates to `peek()`, which lazily evicts an expired entry and increments the `_expirations` counter, so a plain membership test (`key in cache`) mutates cache contents and observability statistics as a side effect instead of being read-only.
paraphrases: Membership testing is not side-effect-free: `key in cache` can delete an expired entry and bump the expiration counter because `__contains__` calls the mutating `peek()`.
Because `__contains__` routes through `peek`, repeatedly checking `key in cache` changes `_expirations` and can evict entries, so containment checks are observably impure.
A read-only `in` check unexpectedly mutates state here — `__contains__` should test presence/liveness without removing keys or updating statistics.
defects.rationale: Correct form: `__contains__` tests key presence and liveness without evicting or touching `_expirations` (no call into the mutating peek()). Human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12 (promoted from a flagged gray zone).
